title: Arguments at home
hook: Jacob walks back toward the brother he cheated: the cooling breath, then the repair face to face
tomorrow: one sister served, one sat and listened. which one got it right?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: wash the bowl. Joshu sent a new monk to the sink. Today, what happens when the sink starts a fight.

segments.voice: Years after he tricked his brother out of their father's blessing, Jacob is walking toward him, and Esau is coming with four hundred men. Jacob has sent gifts ahead. Now he goes in front of his family and bows to the ground seven times as he comes near his brother. Then Esau runs to meet him, embraces him, falls on his neck and kisses him, and they weep. And Jacob says the strangest thing to the brother he wronged: "I have seen thy face, as though I had seen the face of God." Why say that to Esau?
screen: `YEARS AFTER THE TRICK.` → `SEVEN BOWS.` → `THY FACE, AS THE FACE OF GOD.`

segments.voice: Because of the night before. Alone by the ford of the Jabbok, Jacob wrestled with a man until daybreak, and named the place Peniel: "for I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved." One night, in Jacob's words, he sees God face to face. The next morning he sees his brother's face. The two faces rhyme. Jewish law turns that kind of meeting into a rule. The Mishnah says Yom Kippur, the Day of Atonement, atones for wrongs between a person and God, but for wrongs between a person and another person, the day doesn't atone until you make it right with them. Prayer can't go around the person. That's teshuvah, return, with a home address: you go to the one you hurt. Jacob had sent messengers and gifts ahead, but he doesn't stop there. He walks, bows, and asks Esau to accept his gift. So that's why Esau's face feels like God's: repair goes through the other person's face, not around it. At home, after a fight, the cooling breath matters. Then comes the walk back toward the face you argued with.
screen: `I HAVE SEEN GOD FACE TO FACE.` · `TWO FACES THAT RHYME.` · `YOM KIPPUR CAN'T SKIP THE PERSON.` · `TESHUVAH: GO TO THE ONE YOU HURT.` · then, large: `REPAIR.`
